tips.en: Drink 6-8 glasses of clean water through the day, more in hot weather.
tips.hi: दिन भर में 6-8 गिलास साफ पानी पिएँ, गर्मी में और ज़्यादा।
tips.mr: दिवसभरात 6-8 ग्लास स्वच्छ पाणी प्या, उन्हाळ्यात अधिक.

tips.en: Wash your hands with soap for 20 seconds before eating and after using the toilet.
tips.hi: खाने से पहले और शौचालय के बाद 20 सेकंड तक साबुन से हाथ धोएँ।
tips.mr: जेवणापूर्वी आणि शौचालयानंतर 20 सेकंद साबणाने हात धुवा.

tips.en: Adults need about 7-8 hours of sleep. Keep a regular sleep time.
tips.hi: वयस्कों को लगभग 7-8 घंटे की नींद चाहिए। सोने का समय नियमित रखें।
tips.mr: प्रौढांना सुमारे 7-8 तास झोप हवी. झोपेची वेळ नियमित ठेवा.

tips.en: A 30-minute brisk walk on most days helps your heart, mood and weight.
tips.hi: अधिकतर दिनों में 30 मिनट तेज़ चलना दिल, मन और वज़न के लिए अच्छा है।
tips.mr: बहुतेक दिवशी 30 मिनिटे वेगाने चालणे हृदय, मन आणि वजनासाठी चांगले आहे.

tips.en: Fill half your plate with vegetables and fruits at meals.
tips.hi: भोजन में आधी थाली सब्ज़ियों और फलों से भरें।
tips.mr: जेवणात अर्धे ताट भाज्या आणि फळांनी भरा.

tips.en: Take short screen breaks: every 20 minutes look at something far away for 20 seconds.
tips.hi: स्क्रीन से छोटे ब्रेक लें: हर 20 मिनट में 20 सेकंड दूर देखें।
tips.mr: स्क्रीनमधून छोटे ब्रेक घ्या: दर 20 मिनिटांनी 20 सेकंद दूर पाहा.

tips.en: Feeling stressed? Try slow deep breathing for 5 minutes, and talk to someone you trust.
tips.hi: तनाव हो रहा है? 5 मिनट धीरे-धीरे गहरी साँस लें और किसी भरोसेमंद व्यक्ति से बात करें।
tips.mr: ताण वाटतोय? 5 मिनिटे हळू दीर्घ श्वास घ्या आणि विश्वासू व्यक्तीशी बोला.

articles.title: Staying hydrated
articles.summary: Why water matters and how to know you are drinking enough.
body: Water helps your body control temperature, move nutrients and remove waste. Most healthy adults do well with 6-8 glasses of fluids a day, and more in hot weather or when exercising.
Pale-yellow urine usually means you are well hydrated. Dark urine, headache, dry mouth or feeling dizzy can be signs you need more fluids.
Plain water, buttermilk, coconut water and clear soups all count. Limit sugary drinks.
People with kidney or heart conditions should ask their doctor how much fluid is right for them.

articles.title: Better sleep habits
articles.summary: Simple routines that help you fall asleep and wake up refreshed.
body: Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day, even on holidays.
Keep the room dark, quiet and cool. Avoid phone and TV screens for 30-60 minutes before bed.
Avoid heavy meals, tea or coffee late in the evening.
If you regularly cannot sleep, feel very sleepy in the day, or snore loudly with pauses in breathing, speak to a doctor.

articles.title: Looking after your heart
articles.summary: Everyday habits that lower the risk of heart disease.
body: Be active: aim for about 150 minutes of moderate activity a week, such as brisk walking.
Eat less salt, fried food and sweets; eat more vegetables, fruit, pulses and whole grains.
Do not smoke or chew tobacco. Limit alcohol.
Get your blood pressure, blood sugar and cholesterol checked regularly, especially after age 30-40 or if heart disease runs in your family.

articles.title: Hand hygiene and infection prevention
articles.summary: The simplest way to prevent many common infections.
body: Wet your hands, apply soap, rub all surfaces for at least 20 seconds, rinse and dry with a clean cloth or tissue.
Wash before preparing or eating food, after using the toilet, after coughing or sneezing, and after caring for a sick person.
Cover your mouth and nose with a tissue or your elbow when you cough or sneeze.
Stay home when you have a fever so you do not spread infection.

articles.title: Caring for your mental wellbeing
articles.summary: Small steps to manage stress and when to ask for help.
body: Everyone feels stressed sometimes. Regular sleep, physical activity, time with friends and family, and time to relax all help.
Talking about your feelings with someone you trust can make a real difference.

If sadness, worry or hopelessness lasts for more than two weeks, affects your daily life, or you think about harming yourself, please see a doctor or counsellor, or contact a local helpline right away.

faqs.q: Does the chatbot give a diagnosis or prescribe medicine?
faqs.a: No. The chatbot gives general health information and suggests which type of doctor to see. It cannot diagnose diseases or prescribe medicines. Always consult a qualified doctor for your own health decisions.

faqs.q: How do I book an appointment?
faqs.a: Create a free account, open 'Book Appointment', choose a specialty, date and time, and add the reason for your visit. You will see a confirmation immediately and get a notification.

faqs.q: Can I change or cancel my appointment?
faqs.a: Yes. Open 'My Appointments' and use Reschedule or Cancel next to any upcoming appointment.
Passwords are stored as secure hashes, never as plain text, and your appointments and chat history are visible only to you when you are logged in.

faqs.q: What should I do in an emergency?
faqs.a: Call your local emergency number immediately (see the Emergency page) or go to the nearest hospital. Do not use this website or the chatbot to wait for help.

faqs.q: Where does the hospital information come from?
faqs.a: Hospital locations come from OpenStreetMap, a community map. Details such as phone numbers may be missing or out of date, and we do not show live bed or doctor availability. Please call the hospital to confirm.

faqs.q: Why can't I see dosage for medicines?
faqs.a: Correct dosage depends on age, weight, other illnesses and other medicines. To keep you safe we only show general uses, common side effects and precautions. Ask your doctor or pharmacist for the right dose.
The chatbot works in English, Hindi and Marathi. Use the language selector in the chat window.
